assessments.reasoning: The dated and approved SDC field note names Jules I. Schwartz and repeats its report number in page headers. The title has an open-publication restriction, and its introduction identifies the same-date interpreter scope. The fresh PDF hash and every associated raw page, image and content object range match. The cited physical pages were rerendered and inspected at 139 dpi. The displayed passage at FN-LO-34-2, §§2.2 and 2.2.1 Table Definition and Table Declaration Statement, printed pp. 7–8 / PDF pp. 7–8 addresses the proposition. The note in §2.2 narrows the treatment to fixed-length entries. In §2.2.1 the V/R field controls whether the entry count varies, and the count specified with V is the maximum rather than the table's current entry count. The assessment stays within the named dated SDC document and its scope. It assesses documentary wording, not execution on a specific implementation. Fixed-length entries still permit a varying number of entries. The V control word can hold the actual current count separately. The following shorthand can inherit V/R and count from an earlier table, which leaves the stated meanings unchanged. Variable-length entries are explicitly directed to another section.

challenge.method: Compare the §2.2 note with the table form and its V, R and #ENTRIES explanations. Look at the current-count control word and the following identical-table shorthand for apparent alternative interpretations.

limitations: This claim concerns the February 1, 1960 field note and its described profile.
A varying count of fixed-length entries is a different case from variable-length entries, which the manual treats separately. Memory layout and the run-time control word are outside the claim.
The claim gives the declaration field's meaning in the fixed-entry-length case. It does not assert any control-word representation or universal fields for all table forms.
